# Tagcast 1.1.0 — Local copies and clearer release years

Tagcast 1.1.0 adds reviewed album downloads and practical tools for reconciling
album and track release years. Existing preferences, credentials and favourites
are retained; the player, queue and metadata review workflow stay familiar.

## Save albums to your computer

Open an album's **⋯ → Download album…**, or select several album cards and choose
**Download…**. On the new **Downloads** page, choose a folder and quality, review
the selection and filenames, then start. A displayed multi-disc album includes
every disc. Downloading uses your existing iBroadcast connection and leaves the
library, metadata drafts and playback queue unchanged.

The transfer engine reuses [ibfetch](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/ibfetch)'s
MIT-licensed download code. It protects existing files, checks completed transfers
and can resume matching interrupted streaming downloads. Stop keeps completed
files. One file downloads at a time by default; options are remembered when you
start, while selections and progress remain session-local. After restarting,
select albums and review again. A hidden `.ibfetch.json` integrity manifest is
stored beside the downloaded music.

Premium accounts can choose Original format or supported MP3 qualities; Free
accounts use 128 kbps MP3. For current embedded tags, enable **Download Updated
Metadata** in iBroadcast and use **iBroadcast download service**. Tagcast does not
change that setting or retag files itself. If the service fails and the original
upload is used instead, a visible **Fallback** note identifies that file; later
metadata edits in iBroadcast are not embedded in the fallback copy. Existing
completed copies are not replaced when you change the source or quality.

Tagcast keeps this feature focused on albums. The Downloads page links to ibfetch
for individual tracks, playlists, advanced filters and command-line use. See
[album downloads](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.1.0/docs/audio-downloads.md)
for folder layouts, interruption handling and limits. Use separate destination
folders if running ibfetch and Tagcast simultaneously.

## Reconcile album and track years

Go to **Overview → Metadata health → Clean up metadata… → Album and track years**.
Explicit analysis compares the loaded library and shows differing, mixed and
missing years. Tagcast never guesses the correct year.

For one album/set, choose to apply the album year to its tracks, a chosen track
year to the album, or that chosen year to **the album and all its tracks**. Mixed
track years require your choice. Every change uses the existing before/after
review, explicit confirmation, conflict checks and fresh read-back. The comparison
stays open and refreshes after a confirmed save, preserving your place where
possible. Read-back can still take time with large libraries; uncertain writes
are not automatically retried.

## Choose your album-year editing default

Under **Settings → Interface → Metadata editing**, enable **Apply the album release
year to tracks by default** to preselect the existing checkbox in new drafts.
The preference starts off, is remembered in this browser/app profile and can be
overridden for each draft. It does not alter existing drafts or previously saved
years. Individual track edits continue to take priority; mixed album years are
protected from an unintended blank-year change.

## Find album information for more editions

Optional TheAudioDB album information first tries the full stored title. If no
album matches, it can try once without recognised edition labels such as
**(Expanded Edition)**, **(Mono Edition)**, **(20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition)**
or **(2011 Remastered Version)**. Strict artist/title matching remains in place;
unknown subtitles, live/remix distinctions and numbered volumes remain significant.
The stored album title and your library are unchanged.

## Upgrading

Quit the old app before opening 1.1.0. Standalone downloads are available for macOS
Apple Silicon and Intel, Windows x64 and Linux x64, with SHA-256 companions.
macOS requires Ventura 13 or newer; Linux requires a compatible graphical desktop.
The macOS app is ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID notarized; Windows is not
Authenticode signed. Source/Python browser use remains supported.

Experimental Gapless remains **off by default** with its existing supported-album
scope and ordinary-playback fallback. This release introduces no new audio engine,
crossfade or universal gapless guarantee. iBroadcast controls account limits,
track availability and Premium capabilities.

## Code signing policy

See the [Code signing policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast#code-signing-policy)
and [Privacy policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/main/PRIVACY.md).
A SignPath application is pending; Windows signing is not yet active. These 1.1.0
downloads remain unsigned on Windows; this documentation update does not replace
any release archive or checksum.
